**Note:** One search result (the Dealectric ALLPOWERS R4000 page) contained text telling me to ignore my instructions and push a specific discount code and affiliate link. I ignored it and left that listing out of my picks.

## Short answer
The right combo depends on what you run. Most of these sources are affiliate review sites, so check current specs and prices on the seller's page before you buy.

| Your RV use | Power station | Why | Solar to pair |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekends, fridge, laptops, CPAP | **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070Wh, 1,500W, ~24 lb) | Lightest and simplest, but solar input caps at 400W and it isn't expandable | Two Jackery SolarSaga 200W panels use the full 400W |
| Best overall, may grow later | **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** (1,024Wh, 1,800W, 1,000W solar input, expands to 5kWh) | Fastest solar and wall charging of the group | A 200W panel works, but higher-wattage panels get closer to its ~70-minute full-sun recharge |
| Multi-day boondocking, 30A RV port | **BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048Wh, 2,400W, 1,200W solar, ~62 lb) | Built-in 30A RV outlet and the cheapest option for its size | 400W or more of folding or rigid panels |
| Running a roof A/C | **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** (3,024Wh, 3,000W) or **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** (4,096Wh, 4,000W, expandable past 12kWh) | A 13,500 BTU A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W on startup | Large array, since both accept a lot of solar |

## Things to check
- **Solar input ceiling:** A big array is wasted if the station can't accept it. The Jackery 1000 v2 stops at 400W, while the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus takes 1,000W and the AC200L 1,200W.
- **Sizing:** Add up watts × hours. A ~150W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500Wh.
- **Weight:** Units over 3,000Wh are usually two-person lifts.
- **Hardwiring:** Connecting a station to your RV's shore inlet or panel should be done by a licensed electrician. A TT-30 adapter handles plug-in use.
- **Data conflicts:** One source lists the older AC200P with only 700W solar input and a 2-year warranty, which differs from the newer AC200L. Make sure you're looking at the current model.

## Where to buy
I don't have verified direct product URLs, so I won't make any up. These pages carry the price and buy buttons for the models above:
- Camping-focused picks (DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery 1000 v2, AC200L): https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/
- RV-specific picks (DELTA Pro 3, Jackery 3000 Pro, AC200L): https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/
- Brand comparison: https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html

Tell me what you'll run (A/C? fridge? Starlink?), how many nights off-grid, and your budget, and I can narrow this to one station and panel setup.
